Header: Nilaparvata lugens Stal, local name in Khmer

Prevention: Prepare the nursery away from electric light
Field should be planted at the same period
Avoid planting during outbreaks of brown planthopper
Remove weeds from the field and surroundings
Apply fertilizer appropriately (avoid overdosing with nitrogen fertilizer)
Monitoring: Crescent-shaped white eggs concealed in the midrib or leaf sheath
Brown or white adults feeding near the base of tillers
Use light traps (e.g., an electric bulb or kerosene lamp near a light-colored wall or over a pan of water) at night when rice is prone to planthopper attack.
Do not place lights near seedbeds or fields.
If the light trap is inundated with hundreds of
BPH, it's a signal to check your seedbed or field immediately; then scout every day for the next few weeks
Direct Control: In case of abundance of brown planthoppers, submerge the nursery in water and use a mosquito net to catch brown planthoppers.
Flood the seedbed, for a day, so that only the tips of seedlings are exposed to control
BPH Use botanical pesticide (e.g. fresh neem, lemongrass, ginger) 1 litre/15 litres of water
Preserve beneficial insects by reducing the use of chemical pesticides
Use net or scarf to collect and kill
Restrictions: Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
